newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Jiang says he will abide by Hong Kong laws.
newsitem.headline: China's Jiang says he will abide by Hong Kong laws.

text.p: China's President Jiang Zemin said on Friday that no Chinese leader would be above the law in Hong Kong when Beijing resumes sovereignty of the territory on July 1, including himself.

"I wish to emphasis that in the administration of Hong Kong, no matter how powerful I am, I will act according to the Basic Law of Hong Kong's Special Administrative Region," Jiang told Cable News Network (CNN) in an interview.
"Even myself when I go to Hong Kong I must abide by the laws of Hong Kong," he said in an excerpt ahead of the main broadcast scheduled for 9 p.m. (1300 GMT).
Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, becomes a Special Administrative Region of China at midnight on June 30.

Beijing has pledged the territory of 6.4 million people would keep its freewheeling capitalist way of life intact for 50 years after the handover, a promise codified in the Basic Law, Hong Kong's post-colonial constitution promulgated by China in 1990.
